Epher
EE-fer
n. (proper, a grandson of Abraham by Keturah; Hebrew, a calf)
Hebrew Epher, a young deer or calf. Two men bear it: a son of Midian in the line of Keturah, and a man in the genealogy of Judah in Chronicles.

Biblical Definition

The line of Keturah is traced two generations: “And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah” (Genesis 25:4), which the Chronicler repeats almost verbatim: “And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah” (1 Chronicles 1:33). Midian is the significant name in that list. It is the people among whom Moses spent forty years, whose priest Jethro gave him a wife and, later, the best administrative counsel in the Pentateuch; and it is the people whose princes Gideon pursued and whose day of slaughter Isaiah remembers. A second Epher appears among the sons of Ezra in Judah's register (1 Chronicles 4:17). The genealogies keep both, because a register that drops the ordinary man is no register.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a son of Midian in the line of Keturah, and as a man in the genealogy of Judah.

MIDIAN, n. A son of Abraham by Keturah, and the people descended from him, dwelling east and south of Canaan.

CALF, n. The young of the cow kind, or of the bovine genus of quadrupeds.

REGISTER, n. A written account or entry of acts, judgments or proceedings, for preserving and conveying knowledge.

KINDRED, n. Relation by birth; relation by blood; relatives by blood.

COMMON, a. Belonging equally to more than one, or to many indefinitely; usual; ordinary.

Key Scripture

Genesis 25:4 — "And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah."

1 Chronicles 1:33 — "And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah."

1 Chronicles 4:17 — "And the sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon: and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa."

Exodus 18:1 — "When Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father in law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, and that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt;"

Modern Corruption

Wisdom is expected only from inside the household of faith, and Scripture records Israel's best piece of practical governance coming from a Midianite priest who told Moses he would surely wear away.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The instructive thing about Epher's line is where it leads. The sons of Midian are Keturah's grandsons, sent east away from Isaac, and out of Midian comes Jethro, the priest who heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel, rejoiced, offered sacrifice, and then watched Moses judge the people from morning to evening and told him plainly: The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee. The elders, the rulers of thousands and of hundreds, the whole structure of delegated judgment, came from that conversation.

Two guardrails belong here, because Midian is also the nation whose daughters seduced Israel at Baal-peor and against whom God commanded war. Common grace is real, and the church should receive good counsel about ordering her work wherever it comes from; but doctrine and worship are not open to the same borrowing, and Midian is the standing proof that a people who gave wise counsel in one generation led Israel into whoredom in another. Take the counsel; keep the pattern of worship from God alone.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Epher (H6081), a calf; Midyan (H4080), Midian, strife; Yithrow (H3503), Jethro; Qetuwrah (H6989), Keturah.

expand to see more

Hebrew Epher (H6081) — Epher, a calf or young deer; a son of Midian.

Hebrew Midyan (H4080) — Midian, strife; Keturah's son and the people of his name.

Hebrew Yithrow (H3503) — Jethro, his excellence; the priest of Midian, Moses' father in law.

Hebrew Qetuwrah (H6989) — Keturah; all these were the children of Keturah.

Hebrew sar (H8269) — a ruler; rulers of thousands and hundreds, from Jethro's counsel.

Usage

"“The sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher” — Keturah's grandsons."

"“All these were the children of Keturah” — the register closed."

"“The sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher” — a second man kept."
